audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may value trapped or operating cash at par
audit_findings.magnitude: $311.0 million of $315.2 million cash and restricted cash was held outside the U.S. at 2026-06-30; $10.4 million estimated unrecognized deferred tax liability; other distributable-cash haircut unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces the $314.836 million cash add-back in the equity bridge for extraction taxes, legally restricted funds, and minimum operating cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company estimates that it has approximately $ 10.4 million of unrecognized deferred tax liabilities related to any remaining undistributed permanently reinvested foreign earnings that have not already been subject to applicable foreign income tax or local withholding tax on distributions.
audit_findings.explanation: A full $314.836 million overstatement is not demonstrated, and prior repatriations show that foreign cash is not automatically trapped. However, 98.8% of cash and restricted cash was held abroad, an additional $10.4 million extraction-tax liability was estimated, and no minimum operating-cash analysis supports treating the entire balance as surplus. The add-back represents 33.6% of base equity value, so the unresolved availability question is reasonably capable of materially changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cash by legal entity and jurisdiction at 2026-06-30, identify restricted and minimum operating balances, calculate taxes and other leakage on feasible distributions, and rerun the bridge using only net distributable surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 capex anchor may be below near-term economic requirements
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest 12-month guidance is $80-$90 million, $44.4-$54.4 million above 2025 PP&E additions of $35.6 million; the difference equals approximately 100%-123% of the $44.2 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher maintenance or growth-supporting capital expenditures reduce anchor OE or the forecast OE generated by the growth scenarios.
audit_findings.evidence: During the next 12 months, we believe our capital expenditures will be approximately $60 million to $70 million, principally for machinery and equipment to help increase our production capacity to support anticipated revenue growth and our ongoing business around the globe.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a major increase in planned spending, with the latest 10-Q raising guidance beyond the earlier $60-$70 million range. It does not establish how much is maintenance, temporary capacity expansion, or growth investment. Nevertheless, the spending gap is as large as or larger than the entire OE anchor, and the DCF grows that anchor without an identified incremental reinvestment charge, making the issue materially capable of overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 and 2026 capex by project and classify maintenance, replacement, and growth capacity; map growth capex to the scenario growth it supports; then rerun OE with maintenance capex and any required growth reinvestment explicitly charged.

audit_findings.title: Receivables sales can masquerade as recurring owner earnings or excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Unquantified; filed 2025 receivables sales were $627.4 million for $623.6 million of proceeds under a $200.0 million capacity program
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes in receivables outstanding under the sale program alter operating cash flow and period-end cash, potentially distorting historical OE and the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, 2024 and 2023 , the Company sold $ 627.4 million, $ 600.0 million and $ 565.4 million, respectively, of accounts receivable under this program, and in exchange, the Company received cash proceeds of $ 623.6 million, $ 595.9 million and $ 560.9 million, respectively, net of the discount.
audit_findings.explanation: The gross volume sold is demonstrated but does not itself measure an OE distortion because receivables may be sold and replenished repeatedly. The relevant amount is the change in outstanding sold receivables between measurement dates, which is not supplied. Increased utilization would overstate recurring OE or surplus cash, while decreased utilization would have the opposite effect. The record therefore cannot establish the magnitude or direction of the valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain outstanding sold-receivable balances at every year-end and at 2026-06-30, reconstruct utilization changes, neutralize those changes in each OE year, and remove any financing-derived cash remaining in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Known tax-holiday expirations are not explicit in the growth cases
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 tax benefit was $7.576 million, including $5.947 million from Thailand and $1.629 million from China, equal to 17.1% of the $44.2 million OE anchor; 2026 first-half benefit was $2.754 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Expiration raises cash taxes and lowers forecast OE, including terminal-period OE, unless incentives are renewed or replaced.
audit_findings.evidence: The tax incentives in Thailand will expire on December 31, 2030 .
audit_findings.explanation: The benefits and expiration dates are filed, while the valuation uses smooth OE growth and a perpetual terminal value without explicit tax step-ups. China expires after 2026; the latest 10-Q reports Thailand incentives expiring at various dates through 2031, updating the 2030 date in the finding evidence. Because the 2025 benefit is 17.1% of anchor OE and the terminal value extends beyond both expirations, omission is materially capable of overstating value. Renewal or replacement remains uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Rerun every scenario with the China benefit removed beginning in 2027 and each Thailand benefit removed on its latest filed expiration schedule through 2031; separately present any renewal case supported by enacted approvals or executed incentive agreements.

audit_findings.title: The latest anchor contains material discrete tax noise
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed discrete tax expense of $10.4 million, equal to 23.5% of the $44.2 million anchor; if fully embedded and simply reversed, computed gross operating-PV sensitivity is approximately $110.6 million/$2.94 per share in bear, $146.1 million/$3.89 per share in base, and $163.1 million/$4.34 per share in bull
audit_findings.mechanism: A discrete charge embedded in anchor OE is compounded through forecast growth and terminal value; normalization must also remain consistent with repatriation-tax deductions from the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in the effective tax rate in 2025 is primarily due to the $10.4 million in discrete tax expense recorded in the second quarter for the foreign withholding taxes on repatriated distributions and recognition of deferred tax liabilities on China unremitted earnings, losses generated in jurisdictions where no tax benefit can be recognized and to the mix of profits in our various jurisdictions.
audit_findings.explanation: The $10.4 million discrete expense is demonstrated, but the record supplied does not trace precisely how much remains in the $44.2 million OE calculation. Carrying it forward would understate normalized value. Reversing it without a sustainable charge for future withholding and repatriation costs could instead overstate value. Its size relative to anchor OE and the resulting DCF sensitivity make the required normalization material.
audit_findings.action: Trace every component of the $10.4 million through net income and the OE build, separate one-time tax recognition from recurring cash taxes, establish a sustainable jurisdictional cash-tax rate, reconcile it to the foreign-cash haircut, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The stated dilution ceiling conflicts with the filing's maximum PSU payout
audit_findings.magnitude: Conservative maximum incremental dilution of 0.193 million shares, calculated as 0.5 times the 0.386 million PSU target balance at 2026-06-30; 0.51% of the 37.595933 million valuation share count and approximately $0.11-$0.14 per share across scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: Any legacy PSU awards capped at 2.5 times target rather than 2.0 times target increase the fully diluted share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of performance-based restricted stock units that will ultimately be earned will not be determined until the end of the corresponding performance periods and may vary from as low as zero to as high as 2.5 times the target number depending on the level of achievement of certain performance goals.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 10-K supports a 2.5-times ceiling, while the latest 10-Q states that 2025 and 2026 grants are capped at 2.0 times, leaving only a possible legacy-award mismatch. Even assuming conservatively that every 0.386 million target PSU outstanding at 2026-06-30 were affected, the omitted 0.193 million shares would increase the valuation denominator by only 0.51% and reduce scenario values by roughly $0.11-$0.14 per share. That scale cannot materially alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the contractual cap for each remaining legacy PSU grant and add 0.5 times target only for grants retaining the 2.5-times provision; update the diluted-share schedule without changing other valuation inputs.
